questions.question: Which of the following age durations is considered as Early Adulthood stage of human life?

options.text: Begins with the onset of puberty until 18 years
Starts around 25 years until around 45 years
Starts at 6 years and continues till the onset of puberty

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Starts around 18 years until 25 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Early Adulthood** is considered the phase between **18 years to 25 years**, characterized by significant physical, psychological, and social development.
 
• This stage marks the transition from **adolescence to adulthood**, where individuals assume greater responsibilities and begin independent living.
 
• During this stage, individuals often focus on **career development**, pursuing higher education, and forming meaningful relationships.
 
• The **brain's prefrontal cortex** continues to mature during early adulthood, enhancing decision-making, planning, and emotional regulation.
 
• Physical development reaches its peak, with individuals achieving their **maximum strength and physical fitness** during this period.
 
• Early adulthood is also a time for exploring personal values, identity, and long-term goals, contributing to overall **self-actualization**.
 
• This stage is considered critical for establishing a foundation for future life stages, including middle adulthood and old age.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Begins with the onset of puberty until 18 years**__

 __
 
• This stage is referred to as **Adolescence**, which marks the transition from childhood to adulthood.
 
• Adolescence is characterized by significant **physical, hormonal, and emotional changes** due to puberty.
 
• Individuals in this stage experience **growth spurts**, development of secondary sexual characteristics, and heightened emotional sensitivity.
 
• It is also a time for developing **identity**, building social connections, and preparing for adult roles.
 
 
 
• **Starts around 25 years until around 45 years**__
 __
 
• This phase is termed **Middle Adulthood**, marked by increased focus on **career, family, and societal contributions**.
 
• Physical changes, such as **declining metabolism** and potential onset of health issues, begin during this stage.
 
• Individuals in middle adulthood often experience **life stability** but may also face challenges like the "midlife crisis."
 
• It is a critical stage for planning for **retirement** and creating a legacy.
 
 
 
• **Starts at 6 years and continues till the onset of puberty**__
 
 
• This stage is referred to as **Middle Childhood**.
 
• Middle Childhood is a time of steady physical growth and cognitive development, including enhanced **problem-solving skills** and logical thinking.
 
• Social relationships expand, and children develop a stronger sense of **self-esteem** and emotional regulation.
 
• This stage lays the foundation for adolescence by fostering critical skills such as **communication and teamwork**.

questions.question: The Gangaur festival of Rajasthan, which is devoted to Goddess Parvati, lasts for _____ days.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gangaur festival is a major celebration in Rajasthan dedicated to Goddess Parvati.
 
• This festival is particularly significant for women, who pray for marital bliss and the well-being of their husbands.
 
• It is an 18-day long festival that begins the day after Holi and continues until the third day of the Shukla Paksha in Chaitra month.
 
• During the festival, women decorate their hands and feet with intricate Mehndi designs and adorn themselves in traditional attire.
 
• Gangaur involves various rituals, including the making of clay idols of Shiva and Parvati, known as Isar and Gangaur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Significance of Gangaur**

 
 
• Gangaur is celebrated by both married and unmarried women, where married women pray for the well-being and long life of their husbands, and unmarried women seek good spouses.
 
• The festival symbolizes the arrival of spring and harvest.
 
 
 
• **Rituals and Traditions**
 
 
• Women observe fasts, sing traditional songs, and participate in processions carrying the idols of Isar and Gangaur.
 
• On the final day, the idols are immersed in water bodies as a ritualistic farewell to the deities.
 
 
 
• **Mehndi and Attire**
 
 
• Application of Mehndi is a crucial part of the festival, symbolizing the marital status and love for their spouses.
 
• Women wear vibrant, traditional outfits and jewelry specific to their regional customs.
 
 
 
• **Regional Variations**
 
 
• While Gangaur is most prominent in Rajasthan, it is also celebrated with variations in states like Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.
 
• Each region has its own unique customs and practices associated with the festival.

questions.question: Malwa plateau lies to the north of the _______ river.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narmada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Malwa Plateau is located in western Madhya Pradesh and southeastern Rajasthan.
 
• It is bounded by the Narmada River to the south, which is one of the major rivers in central India.
 
• The Vindhya Range forms the southern boundary of the Malwa Plateau and lies just north of the Narmada River.
 
• The plateau is known for its fertile black soil, which is conducive to cotton and soybean farming.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narmada River**

 
 
• The Narmada River is the fifth longest river in India and the largest west-flowing river in the country.
 
• It originates from the Amarkantak Plateau in Madhya Pradesh and flows westwards over a length of 1,312 km before draining into the Arabian Sea.
 
• The river is considered sacred in Hinduism and hosts several pilgrimage sites along its course.
 
• Major dams like Sardar Sarovar Dam are built on the Narmada for irrigation, drinking water, and hydroelectric power.
 
 
 
• **Vindhya Range**
 
 
• The Vindhya Range is a complex, discontinuous chain of mountain ridges, hill ranges, plateau escarpments in west-central India.
 
• It runs roughly parallel to the Narmada River in a west-east direction.
 
• The range is traditionally considered to be the boundary between northern and southern India.
 
• It has a significant influence on the climate and river systems in the region.
 
 
 
• **Malwa Plateau**
 
 
• The Malwa Plateau is part of the Deccan Plateau, one of the oldest and most stable landmasses in India.
 
• The plateau covers an area of approximately 81,767 square kilometers.
 
• It is known for its rich cultural heritage and historical significance, with cities like Ujjain and Indore being major urban centers.
 
• The region's economy is predominantly agrarian, with significant contributions from industries like textiles, chemicals, and pharmaceuticals.
 
 
 
• **Geological Significance**
 
 
• The Malwa Plateau is characterized by volcanic origin and is part of the Deccan Traps, which is one of the largest volcanic features on Earth.
 
• It features extensive basaltic lava flows that date back to the Cretaceous period.
 
• These geological formations are essential for understanding the volcanic history and processes in the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: Which festival is dedicated to the worship of Lord Jagannath?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rath Yatra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rath Yatra** is a major Hindu festival dedicated to the worship of **Lord Jagannath** (a form of Krishna).
 
• This festival is primarily celebrated in the **city of Puri** in the state of Odisha, India.
 
• The Rath Yatra involves the procession of deities Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra on giant chariots from the Jagannath Temple to the **Gundicha Temple**.
 
• The festival takes place annually during the **month of Ashadha** (June or July) in the Hindu calendar.
 
• Millions of devotees gather to participate and witness the event, which symbolizes the journey of the deities to their aunt's house.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jagannath Temple:**

 
 
• Located in Puri, Odisha, it is one of the **Char Dham pilgrimage sites** in India.
 
• The temple is renowned for its unique **architecture** and the annual Rath Yatra.
 
• It was constructed in the 12th century AD by the King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva.
 
 
 
• **Chariots:**
 
 
• The three chariots used in Rath Yatra are called **Nandighosa** (Jagannath's chariot), **Taladhwaja** (Balabhadra's chariot), and **Darpadalana** (Subhadra's chariot).
 
• These chariots are constructed anew every year with wood from specific trees like Phassi and Dhaura.
 
 
 
• **Gundicha Temple:**
 
 
• Also known as the **Garden House of Jagannath**, this temple is the destination of the Rath Yatra procession.
 
• It is believed to be the birthplace of Lord Jagannath.
 
• The deities stay here for seven days before returning to the Jagannath Temple.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The Rath Yatra symbolizes the **annual journey** of Lord Jagannath, his brother Balabhadra, and sister Subhadra to their aunt's house.
 
• It is a **public procession** where devotees can have darshan of the deities outside the temple.
 
• The event is an **expression of unity and equality** as people from all walks of life participate.

questions.question: Which Finance Minister in 1991 initiated a series of reforms that freed up the Indian economy and put the country on a strong growth path?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manmohan Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dr. Manmohan Singh, as the Finance Minister of India, initiated a series of economic reforms in 1991.
 
• These reforms were aimed at liberalizing the Indian economy, reducing the fiscal deficit, and encouraging foreign investment.
 
• The reforms included measures such as devaluation of the Indian rupee, dismantling of the License Raj, and reduction of import tariffs.
 
• These initiatives are credited with transforming the Indian economy and leading to a period of significant growth and globalization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **License Raj**

 
 
• The License Raj refers to the system of elaborate licenses, regulations, and accompanying red tape that were required to set up and run businesses in India between 1947 and 1990.
 
• The 1991 reforms significantly reduced the bureaucratic control over businesses, leading to increased industrial growth.
 
 
 
• **Devaluation of the Indian Rupee**
 
 
• In 1991, the Indian government devalued the rupee to address the balance of payments crisis and improve export competitiveness.
 
• This measure was aimed at making Indian goods cheaper in the global market and boosting foreign exchange reserves.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**
 
 
• The reforms opened up various sectors of the economy to foreign direct investment, which was previously restricted.
 
• This led to increased capital inflow, technology transfer, and global integration of the Indian economy.
 
 
 
• **Reduction of Import Tariffs**
 
 
• The 1991 reforms included significant reduction in import tariffs, making it cheaper to import goods and services.
 
• This move was aimed at increasing competition and improving the quality of domestic products.

questions.question: In which of the following regions is the Karakoram Range located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Northern India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Karakoram Range is a large mountain range spanning the borders of Pakistan, India, and China.
 
• It is located in the northern part of the Indian subcontinent, primarily in the regions of Gilgit-Baltistan (administered by Pakistan) and Ladakh (administered by India).
 
• This range is home to some of the world's highest peaks, including K2, the second highest mountain in the world.
 
• The Karakoram Range is part of a complex mountain system that includes the Himalayas and the Hindu Kush ranges.
 
• The range is also known for its extensive glacial systems, including the Siachen Glacier, one of the longest glaciers outside the polar regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical Significance:**

 
 
• The Karakoram Range forms part of the boundary between the Indian subcontinent and the Eurasian landmass.
 
• It plays a crucial role in influencing the climate and hydrology of the region.
 
 
 
• **Glaciers and Rivers:**
 
 
• The range contains some of the most extensive glacial systems in the world, contributing significantly to river systems such as the Indus.
 
• The meltwater from these glaciers is a critical water source for millions of people in the downstream regions.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Diversity:**
 
 
• The Karakoram Range is known for its unique biodiversity, including rare and endangered species such as the snow leopard.
 
• The high-altitude ecosystems in this region are fragile and sensitive to environmental changes.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• The range has significant strategic importance due to its location at the tri-junction of Pakistan, India, and China.
 
• It has been a site of military presence and activity, particularly in areas like the Siachen Glacier.

questions.question: Which of the following countries signed a bilateral Customs Cooperation Arrangement agreement in August 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India and New Zealand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India and New Zealand signed a bilateral Customs Cooperation Arrangement agreement in August 2024.
 
• The agreement aims to facilitate efficient and secure trade between the two nations.
 
• This cooperation will enhance mutual assistance in customs matters, including the exchange of information and best practices.
 
• The arrangement is expected to strengthen the trade relationship and boost economic ties between India and New Zealand.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Customs Cooperation:**

 
 
• Customs cooperation agreements are international treaties that facilitate trade by simplifying and harmonizing customs procedures.
 
• These agreements promote information sharing, joint training, and mutual assistance in customs enforcement.
 
• They help prevent and combat customs fraud and smuggling activities.
 
• Such cooperation ensures the safety and security of international trade while promoting economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Trade Relations:**
 
 
• Strong trade relations between countries contribute to economic development and job creation.
 
• Bilateral trade agreements often include provisions for reducing tariffs, eliminating trade barriers, and protecting intellectual property rights.
 
• Countries with robust trade relationships tend to have greater political and diplomatic cooperation.
 
• Trade agreements can cover a wide range of sectors including agriculture, manufacturing, services, and technology.
 
 
 
• **Economic Ties:**
 
 
• Economic ties refer to the economic relationships and transactions between countries.
 
• These ties can include trade, investment, and financial exchanges.
 
• Strong economic ties are crucial for global economic stability and growth.
 
• Countries with strong economic ties often collaborate on global economic policies and initiatives.

questions.question: What is one effect of liberalisation in the industrial sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increased competition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Liberalisation in the industrial sector typically results in **increased competition** among businesses.
 
• It allows **foreign companies** to enter the domestic market, providing more choices for consumers and forcing local companies to improve their products and services.
 
• Increased competition can drive **innovation and efficiency** as companies strive to maintain or improve their market position.
 
• It encourages **foreign direct investment (FDI)**, bringing in capital, technology, and expertise from other countries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liberalisation**

 
 
• It refers to the relaxation of government regulations and restrictions in an economy in exchange for greater participation by private entities.
 
• In India, economic liberalisation began in 1991, leading to significant changes in various sectors, including industry.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**
 
 
• FDI is an investment made by a firm or individual in one country into business interests located in another country.
 
• It is a critical driver for economic growth, providing opportunities for job creation, technology transfer, and infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **Innovation**
 
 
• The process of translating an idea or invention into a good or service that creates value or for which customers will pay.
 
• Increased competition often leads to higher levels of innovation as companies seek to differentiate themselves from their competitors.
 
 
 
• **Market Efficiency**
 
 
• A market is efficient when it is able to quickly and accurately incorporate all available information into prices.
 
• Increased competition can lead to higher market efficiency as companies streamline their operations to reduce costs and improve service quality.

questions.question: Slash and Burn agriculture is known as ___________ in Madhya Pradesh.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dahiya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Slash and Burn agriculture, also known as shifting cultivation, is referred to as **Dahiya** in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• This agricultural practice involves the cutting and burning of plants in a forest or woodland to create a field called a swidden.
 
• Post burning, the land is used for agriculture for a few years until the soil's fertility diminishes.
 
• After the land loses its fertility, it is left to regenerate naturally while the farmer moves on to a new plot.
 
• Slash and Burn agriculture is a traditional practice still observed in various parts of India, including the tribal areas of Madhya Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shifting Cultivation**

 
 
• It is an agricultural system in which plots of land are cultivated temporarily, then abandoned while the farmer moves to another plot.
 
• It allows the natural vegetation to restore the fertility of the soil.
 
• Shifting cultivation is commonly practiced in tropical regions around the world.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact**
 
 
• While it can be sustainable in low-population-density areas, shifting cultivation can lead to deforestation and loss of biodiversity.
 
• It can also contribute to soil erosion and degradation if not managed properly.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Practices**
 
 
• Agroforestry, which combines agriculture and forestry techniques, is seen as a sustainable alternative.
 
• Conservation agriculture, which includes minimal soil disturbance and permanent soil cover, is another alternative.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives**
 
 
• The Indian government has various programs aimed at promoting sustainable agriculture and preventing deforestation.
 
• Programs like the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) encourage practices that improve soil health and reduce environmental impact.

• Dependence on monsoon rains makes the crop vulnerable to droughts and water scarcity.
 
• Pests and diseases pose a constant threat to sugarcane crops, requiring effective pest management practices.

questions.question: The Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas (DWCRA) program was launched in the year __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1982**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas (DWCRA) program was launched in **1982** by the Government of India.
 
• The primary objective of DWCRA is to improve the socio-economic status of the poor women in rural areas through the creation of income-generating activities.
 
• DWCRA operates under the broader Integrated Rural Development Program (IRDP).
 
• It emphasizes group formation among women to foster self-employment and income generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Integrated Rural Development Program (IRDP)**

 
 
• IRDP was introduced in 1978 and implemented in 1980 with the aim to provide employment opportunities to the rural poor and to improve their living conditions.
 
• It is a self-employment program focused on providing credit and subsidy to the target group.
 
 
 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**
 
 
• SHGs are small voluntary associations of poor people, preferably from the same socio-economic background.

questions.question: When cotton and rubber are rubbed together, it will result in which of the following?

options.text: Cotton and rubber will be negatively charged.

• Cotton tends to lose electrons and become positively charged.

• **Electron Affinity**

questions.question: The 3rd step of the Carnot cycle is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**reversible isothermal compression**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The third step of the Carnot cycle involves **reversible isothermal compression**, which occurs at a constant temperature.
 
• During this process, **heat is expelled** from the system to the surroundings.
 
• The temperature remains constant while the **volume decreases** and the **pressure increases**.
 
• This step helps in maintaining the cycle's efficiency by **compressing the gas** without any change in temperature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carnot Cycle:**

 
 
• The Carnot cycle is a theoretical thermodynamic cycle proposed by Nicolas Léonard Sadi Carnot in 1824.
 
• It consists of two isothermal processes (one for expansion and one for compression) and two adiabatic processes (one for expansion and one for compression).
 
• It is used to determine the maximum possible efficiency of a heat engine.
 
 
 
• **Isothermal Process:**
 
 
• An isothermal process is one where the temperature remains constant throughout the process.
 
• In an isothermal process, the internal energy of the system remains unchanged.
 
 
 
• **Adiabatic Process:**
 
 
• In an adiabatic process, there is no heat exchange between the system and its surroundings.
 
• The process is characterized by a change in temperature and pressure within the system.
 
 
 
• **Thermodynamic Efficiency:**
 
 
• Thermodynamic efficiency is a measure of how well an engine converts heat into work.
 
• The efficiency of the Carnot cycle is the highest possible efficiency for any heat engine.

questions.question: On 3 February 1925, the first electric train in India ran between which two stations?

__
 
• The first electric train in India ran on **3 February 1925** between Bombay VT (now Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus) and Kurla Harbour.
 
• This marked a significant milestone in the history of the Indian Railways, showcasing the shift from steam to electric traction.
 
• The train service was launched under the British colonial rule to improve the efficiency and speed of rail transport.
 
• Bombay VT, now known as Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), is one of the busiest railway stations in India and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrification of Indian Railways**

 
 
• The electrification of railways in India began in the early 20th century to enhance the efficiency of train operations.
 
• It involves the installation of overhead electric lines and the use of electric locomotives instead of diesel or steam engines.
 
• Electric trains are known for their higher acceleration, greater hauling capacity, and reduced operational costs compared to steam and diesel trains.
 
• As of 2023, Indian Railways aims to achieve 100% electrification of its broad-gauge routes to promote sustainable and eco-friendly transportation.

• Electrification leads to reduced fuel costs and lower maintenance requirements for locomotives.
 
• It contributes to the enhanced safety of train operations through the reduction of fire hazards associated with diesel fuel.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution was amended to include the Right to Education as a Fundamental Right?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 21**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Right to Education was included as a Fundamental Right under Article 21A of the Constitution of India.
 
• This amendment was brought about by the Constitution (86th Amendment) Act, 2002.
 
• Article 21A states that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years.
 
• This amendment came into effect on 1st April 2010.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights**

 
 
• Fundamental Rights are the basic human rights enshrined in the Constitution of India which are guaranteed to all citizens.
 
• They are enforceable by the courts, subject to specific restrictions.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment Act, 2002**
 
 
• This amendment made three specific provisions in the Indian Constitution:
 
• Added Article 21A (Right to Education).
 
• Changed the subject matter of Article 45 (Provision for early childhood care and education to children below the age of six years).
 
• Added a new fundamental duty under Article 51A (k) (It shall be the duty of every citizen of India who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years).
 
 
 
• **Free and Compulsory Education**
 
 
• The term "free education" means that no child is liable to pay any kind of fee or charges or expenses which may prevent him or her from pursuing and completing elementary education.
 
• "Compulsory education" means an obligation of the appropriate government to provide free elementary education and ensure compulsory admission, attendance, and completion of elementary education by every child in the six to fourteen age group.
 
 
 
• **Role of State Governments**
 
 
• The state governments have a crucial role in implementing the right to education.
 
• They are responsible for ensuring that every child in the age group of six to fourteen years is provided free and compulsory education.

questions.question: Articles 36 to 51 containing 'Directive Principles of State Policy' come under which Part of the Constitution?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Articles 36 to 51 are categorized under **Part IV** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy** (DPSP) are enshrined in Part IV, aiming to establish social and economic democracy in the country.
 
• These principles are not enforceable by any court, but the principles laid down are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The Directive Principles act as guidelines for the central and state governments of India to frame laws and policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Context**

 
 
• The concept of Directive Principles was borrowed from the Irish Constitution, which had copied it from the Spanish Constitution.
 
• These principles reflect the ideals that the framers of the Constitution aimed to achieve in the long run.
 
 
 
• **Categories of DPSP**
 
 
• The DPSP are classified into three categories: Socialistic, Gandhian, and Liberal-Intellectual.
 
• Socialistic principles aim to provide social and economic justice, Gandhian principles reflect the ideology of Mahatma Gandhi, and Liberal-Intellectual principles focus on the rights of citizens.
 
 
 
• **Not Justiciable**
 
 
• DPSPs are not enforceable by law, which means they are not justiciable in a court of law.
 
• However, they are fundamental in the governance of the country and it is the duty of the state to apply these principles in making laws.
 
 
 
• **Key Articles**
 
 
• Article 39: Directs the state to secure a social order for the promotion of the welfare of the people.
 
• Article 40: Directs the state to organize village panchayats and endow them with powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.
 
• Article 45: Directs the state to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.

questions.question: What was the average (median) Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) in India from September 1962 to 30 October 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.04**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)** is a crucial monetary policy tool used by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
• From September 1962 to 30 October 2024, the average (median) CRR in India has been **0.04**, which translates to 4%.
 
• CRR is the percentage of a bank's total deposits that must be maintained with the RBI in the form of liquid cash.
 
• The purpose of the CRR is to ensure that banks do not run out of cash to meet the payment demands of their depositors.
 
• Adjustments to the CRR can influence the liquidity and credit conditions in the banking system and are used to control inflation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)**

 
 
• SLR is the percentage of a bank's net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) that must be maintained in the form of gold, cash, or government-approved securities.
 
• It is another monetary policy instrument used by the RBI to control liquidity in the banking system.
 
• The SLR is mandated to ensure the solvency of banks and control the expansion of bank credit.
 
• As of October 2023, the SLR requirement stands at 18.00% of NDTL.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**
 
 
• The MPC is a committee constituted by the Central Government to set the policy interest rate to achieve the inflation target.
 
• It comprises six members - three officials from the RBI and three external members nominated by the Government of India.
 
• The Governor of the RBI is the ex-officio Chairperson of the MPC.
 
• The MPC meets bi-monthly to review and set the repo rate, which influences the CRR and other rates.
 
 
 
• **Repo Rate**
 
 
• The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends money to commercial banks in the event of any shortfall of funds.
 
• It is an instrument of monetary policy used to control inflation and stimulate the economy.
 
• Changes in the repo rate can affect the CRR and the overall liquidity in the banking system.
 
• As of October 2023, the repo rate in India stands at 6.50%.

__
 
• The British policies led to the rapid decline of Indian handicrafts due to the influx of cheaper, mass-produced British goods, which were more affordable than locally made products.
 
• Indian artisans faced severe economic hardship as their products could not compete with the machine-made goods imported from Britain.
 
• The British imposed heavy duties on Indian textiles while allowing free entry of British goods, further crippling the local industries.
 
• The destruction of traditional handicraft industries contributed to widespread unemployment and poverty among Indian artisans and craftsmen.

• **Tariff Policies:** British policies included high tariffs on Indian goods entering Britain while allowing British goods to enter India with minimal or no tariffs, creating an unequal trade environment.

questions.question: Magnetic field lines represent the path along which ______________.

options.text: a hypothetical free south pole would tend to move
a free proton would tend to move

a free electron would tend to move

questions.solution:

__
 
• Magnetic field lines are imaginary lines used to represent the direction and strength of a magnetic field.
 
• The direction of the magnetic field at any point is tangential to the magnetic field line at that point.
 
• A hypothetical free north pole would move along the magnetic field line from the north pole to the south pole of a magnet.
 
• The density of the magnetic field lines indicates the strength of the magnetic field; closer lines signify a stronger field.
 
• Magnetic field lines never intersect each other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic Field**

 
 
• A magnetic field is a vector field that describes the magnetic influence on moving electric charges, electric currents, and magnetic materials.
 
• It can be visualized using magnetic field lines that show the direction and strength of the field.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Poles**
 
 
• Every magnet has two poles: north and south.
 
• Like poles repel each other, while unlike poles attract each other.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetism**
 
 
• Electromagnetism is the interaction between electric currents or fields and magnetic fields.
 
• It is one of the four fundamental forces of nature.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Flux**
 
 
• Magnetic flux is the measure of the quantity of magnetism, considering the strength and the extent of a magnetic field.
 
• It is measured in Weber (Wb).

questions.question: The Swaran Singh Committee recommendation added which of the following to the Indian Constitution?

• **Elephant Corridors:**

 
 
• Elephant corridors are narrow strips of land that connect two large habitats of elephants.
 
• These corridors are crucial for the migration and movement of elephants, helping to maintain their genetic diversity and reduce human-elephant conflict.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Efforts:**
 
 
• Several conservation programs and policies are in place in India to protect elephant corridors, including Project Elephant and various state-level initiatives.

questions.question: Keeping the linear velocity of a particle moving in a circular path constant, as the radius of the circular path decreases, the centripetal acceleration:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Centripetal acceleration is given by the formula **a꜀ = v² / r**, where v is the linear velocity and r is the radius of the circular path.
 
• For a constant linear velocity, as the radius of the circular path decreases, the centripetal acceleration increases.
 
• This is because centripetal acceleration is inversely proportional to the radius of the circular path.
 
• The increased centripetal acceleration implies a higher force required to keep the particle moving in the circular path.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Centripetal Force:**

 
 
• Centripetal force is the force that acts on a body moving in a circular path and is directed towards the center around which the body is moving.
 
• The formula for centripetal force is F꜀ = m * a꜀, where m is the mass of the particle and a꜀ is the centripetal acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Linear Velocity:**
 
 
• Linear velocity refers to the velocity of an object moving along a straight line.
 
• In circular motion, it is the speed at which the particle moves along the circumference of the circle.
 
 
 
• **Angular Velocity:**
 
 
• Angular velocity is the rate of change of the angle through which a particle moves on a circular path.
 
• It is given by the formula ω = v / r, where ω is the angular velocity, v is the linear velocity, and r is the radius.
 
 
 
• **Radius of Curvature:**
 
 
• The radius of curvature is the radius of the circular path along which the particle moves.
 
• It is a measure of the curvature of the path and determines the centripetal force required to maintain circular motion.

questions.question: According to the Constitution of India, who conducts the Election of the Vice-President of India?

options.text: The Legislature Councils of all States
The Legislative Assemblies of all States

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Election Commission of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body responsible for conducting the elections for the Vice-President of India.
 
• The election is held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.
 
• Members of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) participate in the election.
 
• The Election Commission ensures free and fair conduct of the election, adhering to the established legal framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI)**

 
 
• The ECI is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at national and state levels.
 
• It was established on January 25, 1950, and is headquartered in New Delhi.
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) heads the ECI along with other Election Commissioners.
 
• The ECI's primary role is to ensure free, fair, and impartial elections.
 
 
 
• **Vice-President of India**
 
 
• The Vice-President is the second-highest constitutional office in India, ranking right after the President.
 
• The Vice-President also serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• The term of office for the Vice-President is five years.
 
• In the event of the President's resignation, removal, death, or otherwise, the Vice-President may act as the President until a new President is elected.
 
 
 
• **Proportional Representation**
 
 
• It is a type of electoral system in which parties gain seats in proportion to the number of votes cast for them.
 
• This system ensures minority groups receive a fair representation in the legislature.
 
• Proportional representation aims to reflect the diversity of the electorate in the elected body.

questions.question: Which state was carved out of Assam as an autonomous state in 1970?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Meghalaya was carved out of Assam as an autonomous state in **1970** under the Assam Reorganization (Meghalaya) Act, 1969.
 
• It became a full-fledged state on **January 21, 1972**, following the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganization) Act, 1971.
 
• The state was created to provide autonomy to the Khasi, Garo, and Jaintia Hills tribes of the region.
 
• Shillong, the capital city of Meghalaya, was formerly the capital of Assam until the formation of Meghalaya.
 
• Meghalaya is known as the "Abode of Clouds" and is one of the smallest states in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Assam Reorganization (Meghalaya) Act, 1969:** This Act granted Meghalaya the status of an autonomous state within Assam, with its own legislature and executive council.
 
• **North-Eastern Areas (Reorganization) Act, 1971:** This Act reorganized the northeastern states of India, leading to the creation of Meghalaya as a full-fledged state.
 
• **Tribal Groups:** Meghalaya is predominantly inhabited by three major tribal groups - the Khasi, Garo, and Jaintia tribes, who have distinct cultures and traditions.
 
• **Unique Geography:** Meghalaya is characterized by its hilly terrain, heavy rainfall, and lush green landscapes, making it a major tourist destination.
 
• **Languages:** The principal languages spoken in Meghalaya are Khasi, Garo, and English, which is the official language of the state.
